body.statement: On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\), for \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), every \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private estimator satisfies \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}=c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\). The \(r_F\) branch follows by setting \(ab\asymp r_F\), \(h\asymp r_F^{1/\gamma}\), and \(\ell\asymp r_F^{1/q}\) in the component coupling before applying a central-private two-prior testing inequality.
body.justification: The lower bound certifies that both privacy balances are intrinsic to the causal class.
body.gap: Cai et al. establish the direct pointwise-regression privacy barrier, while no published result adds the coupled-nuisance \(n^2\epsilon_n\) branch for CATE.
body.consumer: It prevents private CATE algorithms from being benchmarked only against ordinary private regression.
